content.text: I'm rating this as an FRQ-style item with two parts. Part (a) is the standard digit-extraction loop using % 10 and / 10, which is core 2.9/2.10 content. Part (b) needs a while or for loop that calls digitSum and tests divisibility with %. Its edge cases are mild: start >= 1 guarantees a nonzero digit sum, and the loop terminates because a Harshad number always exists (every number from 1 to 9 qualifies, and so do multiples of 10, 12, and so on). The reading load is small and no long arithmetic is required. The main reasoning is decomposing the problem and correctly reusing the helper method. This matches a typical AP Methods and Control Structures FRQ, so it fits full-mock exam_prep.
